newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CROWN SLIPS AS MARK GAINS GROUND ON DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CROWN SLIPS AS MARK GAINS GROUND ON DOLLAR.

text.p: The Czech crown weakened slightly in early morning activity, pulled down by an upturn in the mark and the carryover effects of some market operations, dealers said.
"We can justify the weakness by the fact that there was a weekend carry operation and therefore the shift in the rate was caused by this," said Petr Korous of bank CSOB.
At 0750 GMT, the crown was trading against the mark at 18.421 after opening at 18.350 and against the dollar at 33.846 after 33.700 at the opening.
Dealers added that a strenghtening in the mark against the dollar was also contributing to the crown's weakness.

But they said the continued high interest rate policy of the central bank should keep the crown in favour with investors who have pushed the currency higher in recent weeks following a major crisis in May which forced the central bank to abandon the crown's +/-7.5 percent dollar/mark fixing.
